head: ACM-68000
Clearance rules and the immutable rule register · Canonical text
Version 1.1 · 31 October 2026 · Standard held by Allooloo Technologies Corp. · Open standard, MIT licence
mission: ACM-68000 defines the clearance rule reference and signal vocabulary for listed issuers' records. Its rule register binds every rule_version used in a receipt to an immutable revision of a duty, its jurisdiction, legal reference, sources and effective dates. Each family publishes how its evidence-backed outcomes map to the clearance signals for a specified read or action. The producing node signs rule and outcome records under the ECO-10060 contract; the RCO door separately signs the receipt of the cleared read. ACM makes the governing revision and the meaning of clearance recoverable, and keeps three distinctions: lookup is not permission, missing evidence is not a negative finding, and system failure is not a resolved restriction.
paragraphs: ACM-200 means cleared. It never means a listing state. A listing attribute — trading, suspended, delisted — belongs in its own field on the record. A sourced halt may be an input to a family's restriction rule; the raw listing attribute and the resolved signal remain distinct, including when both appear in one response.

ACM-404 names the register and the lookup target: an absent rule revision and an absent subject registration are different failures and never share an unexplained message. ACM-451 names the required filing or evidence when known, and never disguises a service outage as a request to read.
binding_paragraphs: The bindings below are the common interpretation. Each immutable family revision supplies its own source-backed prerequisites, applicability and reason codes before a binding is applied. A listed duty name is a register seed, not a completed rule.

An ESG ACM-200 clears the named check; it is not a sustainability claim. An AMP ACM-200 requires route-gate evidence; it is never produced because an endpoint is discoverable. An unresolved prerequisite stays visible: no evaluation issues ACM-200 while hiding an unmet condition. Evidence gaps, operational errors and unresolved conflicts have explicit representations, and a family uses ACM-451 only where its published binding calls for the named source to be read.

ACM-200.boundary: The specified read or action has cleared the applicable registered checks in the stated context.

bindings.outcome: Declared action clears the duty checks
Product, market and client-class action clears the orderability checks
Actor, instrument, action and endpoint clear the route gates
The named disclosure check clears its defined criteria

ACM-403.boundary: Evidence establishes a restriction or an applicable halt under the selected revision.

bindings.outcome: An applicable duty condition restricts the action
Evidence establishes a distribution or target-market restriction
An applicable venue restriction, entitlement failure or halt is established
Evidence establishes a restriction under the applicable disclosure rule

ACM-404.boundary: The named lookup target is absent from the identified register. This establishes neither global absence nor prohibition.

bindings.outcome: Requested duty revision absent from the register
Requested product or rule registration absent from its register
Requested venue, route or rule registration absent from its register
Requested disclosure or rule registration absent from its register

ACM-451.boundary: The binding requires the identified filing or source to be read before a conclusion or a progression.

bindings.outcome: A specified filing must be read to complete the check
Required product or target-market material must be read
Required venue notice or filing must be read
Required disclosure material must be read
